title: Sultan Bell Pepper (Sultan F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Sultan bell pepper is an F1 hybrid bell pepper variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sultan bell pepper is an F1 hybrid bell pepper variety, also sold or known as Sultan F1 or Sultan sweet pepper. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed (also sold by Harbest Agribusiness).

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Sultan bell pepper is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sultan F1 or Sultan sweet pepper, this is the same bell pepper. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [bell pepper variety finder](/crop-varieties/bell-pepper), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 55 to 60 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit bell pepper fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 55 to 60 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Conical sweet pepper, firm, smooth and thick, light green turning red.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: sold in Philippine farm shops under the East West name. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual bell pepper on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Sultan bell pepper

Bell pepper does best in cool places such as Benguet and Bukidnon. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and grow it in the dry season under some shade. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Sultan F1 the same as Sultan?
items.a: Yes. Sultan F1 is another name for Sultan. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sultan?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
